**Verdict**: I’ll **keep** this hand. It’s not perfect, but it has a reasonable curve and strong payoffs. I’ll hope to draw a 1-drop or another land to smooth things out.

annotations.description: Timed out during precombat main phase, missing a critical land drop on turn 5. With expensive cards in hand (Tectonic Giant at 4 mana, Soul Read at 4 mana, Furious Rise at 3 mana), missing this land drop delays the entire game plan by a turn.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — passed without playing Island or casting any spell.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island to go to 3 lands, then pass to hold Brineborn Cutthroat for the opponent's turn (where it gains value from its flash + counter ability). This sets up a turn 6 Tectonic Giant with 4 lands.

annotations.description: Lightning Phoenix provides immediate 2 haste damage but can't block, while Weaver of Lightning (1/4 reach) would better support the slow hand full of expensive cards (Somberwald Stag at 5, Living Lightning at 4, Lightning Diadem at 6) that needs time to deploy. Weaver also synergizes with Irresistible Prey in hand for the ping trigger + card draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Phoenix (2/2 flying haste, can't block)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Weaver of Lightning (1/4 reach) to provide a strong defensive body that buys time to deploy expensive threats, with instant/sorcery ping synergy from Irresistible Prey in hand

annotations.description: Brineborn Cutthroat was cast on MstLg Tinker's own turn, wasting the flash advantage. Casting it during the opponent's next turn would give it a +1/+1 counter from its own ability (making it 3/2 instead of 2/1). The Cutthroat can't block Lightning Phoenix (a flyer) anyway, so there's no defensive urgency to deploy it now.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Brineborn Cutthroat on own turn in response to Lightning Phoenix on the stack
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority here, let Lightning Phoenix resolve, then hold Brineborn Cutthroat to cast during the opponent's turn to get a +1/+1 counter trigger

annotations.description: Blocked Lightning Phoenix with Brineborn Cutthroat, trading a high-upside growing creature for a recursive Phoenix that can return from the graveyard. At 20 life, taking 2 damage is negligible, while Cutthroat had significant growth potential with Soul Read and Synchronized Eviction in hand to cast on opponent's turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Lightning Phoenix (2/2) with Brineborn Cutthroat (2/1), resulting in both dying. Phoenix can recur, Cutthroat cannot.
annotations.betterLine: Don't block. Take 2 damage (going to 18), preserve Brineborn Cutthroat to grow it on future opponent turns with instants in hand. The Cutthroat's long-term value far exceeds 2 life points, especially against a creature that can return from the graveyard.

annotations.description: Player attempted to cast a spell but submitted an invalid mana plan (tapping Thriving Bluff twice), causing the action to be rolled back. This resulted in passing with no action taken despite having castable spells (Burst Lightning for R, or Furious Rise for 2R). The opponent's Lightning Phoenix is on board as a threat that could have been killed with Burst Lightning, and Furious Rise could have been deployed as a card advantage engine.
annotations.actionTaken: No action taken due to failed mana payment (timeout/rollback).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Burst Lightning targeting Lightning Phoenix (using Thriving Bluff for R), killing the 2/2 flyer while keeping UU open. Alternatively, cast Furious Rise (UUR) to set up future card advantage.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Brineborn Cutthroat (2/1) when the opponent has no untapped blockers. Lightning Phoenix can't block, and all opponent's lands are tapped. This is 2 free damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack, passing the combat phase.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Brineborn Cutthroat for 2 free damage. The opponent has no blockers available and no mana to cast anything.

annotations.description: Using Burst Lightning on Lightning Phoenix is inefficient because the Phoenix can recur from the graveyard whenever the opponent deals 3+ damage in a turn. While opponent's lands are tapped now preventing immediate recursion, the Phoenix will likely return in future turns, making this removal temporary. Burst Lightning could be saved for a non-recursive threat or used as reach to close out the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Burst Lightning targeting Lightning Phoenix
annotations.betterLine: Hold Burst Lightning for a more permanent removal target or for face damage as a finisher. The Phoenix is annoying but recurring creatures are poor removal targets. Passing the turn and potentially casting Soul Read or Synchronized Eviction on opponent's turn (at instant speed) to develop card advantage would be more efficient.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Temur Battle Rage (which was rolled back due to mana issues) instead of Furious Rise. Temur Battle Rage on a 2/1 Brineborn Cutthroat would be a poor use of the combat trick even if it resolved - dealing 4 damage to a 20-life opponent while spending a card. Furious Rise would provide ongoing card advantage, especially once Tectonic Giant (4 power, in hand) comes down to trigger it.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Temur Battle Rage, which failed due to mana payment issues, resulting in no action.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Furious Rise for {2}{R} to set up recurring card advantage. With Tectonic Giant in hand as a 4-power creature to enable it, Furious Rise would generate significant value over the coming turns.

annotations.description: Passed with Furious Rise as the only castable spell while opponent is tapped out. While Furious Rise does nothing without a power 4+ creature, deploying it now when opponent can't interact sets up future card advantage once Tectonic Giant (in hand) is cast. The mana would otherwise go unused since there are no other plays available.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 3 untapped lands and no plays made.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Furious Rise now while opponent is tapped out, setting up the enchantment for when Tectonic Giant eventually hits the battlefield. The 3 mana would be wasted anyway since there are no other castable spells.

annotations.description: Equipping Marauder's Axe before casting Irresistible Prey wastes a free draw that could inform the rest of the turn. Both cost the same total mana (Prey costs {G}, Equip costs {2}, total {2}{G} = 3 mana), but casting the cantrip first gives information and potentially draws a land to play, opening up more options like casting Dawntreader Elk as well.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Marauder's Axe (equip) before casting any spells
annotations.betterLine: Cast Irresistible Prey targeting Weaver of Lightning for {G} to draw a card first, then with the drawn card's information (and potentially an extra land drop), decide whether to equip the Axe or take a different line.

annotations.description: Moving Marauder's Axe (likely from Weaver of Lightning to Phoenix) reduces total attack power next turn. Casting Dawntreader Elk instead would add a 2/2 body, providing more total damage (7 vs 5) and ramp potential to cast expensive threats like Somberwald Stag or Lightning Diadem.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Marauder's Axe to re-equip it
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dawntreader Elk for {1}{G}, adding a 2/2 body to the board. This provides more total combat damage next turn and the option to sacrifice it for ramp to cast Somberwald Stag or Lightning Diadem.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Time to Feed targeting Tectonic Giant, but this was rolled back. Beyond the mana issue, targeting Tectonic Giant with Time to Feed would trigger the Giant's ability (dealing 3 damage to GPT5 Gramps or giving the opponent card advantage), making it a costly removal option. Additionally, the player hadn't played their land drop yet - they should play a land first before committing to spells to maximize available mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Time to Feed (rolled back by engine due to mana payment failure)
annotations.betterLine: Play a land drop first (if any land in hand - none visible, so this may not apply). Consider casting Dawntreader Elk or Lightning Visionary instead, saving Time to Feed for when you have more mana or a better fight target. Also note that targeting Tectonic Giant with any spell triggers its 3-damage ability.

annotations.description: At 10 life facing 5 damage from Weaver of Lightning (3/4) and Lightning Phoenix (2/2), the player declined to block with Tectonic Giant (3/4). Blocking Weaver of Lightning would result in both creatures surviving (3 damage to each 4-toughness creature), saving 3 life (taking only 2 from Phoenix instead of 5 total). Going to 5 life instead of 8 is a significant difference, especially with the opponent having 8 cards in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not block, taking 5 damage (10 → 5 life)
annotations.betterLine: Block Weaver of Lightning with Tectonic Giant. Both 3-power/4-toughness creatures survive combat, and you only take 2 damage from Lightning Phoenix (10 → 8 life), preserving a crucial 3 life points.

annotations.description: Passed precombat main phase without playing Mountain from hand. Opponent is at 5 life with all lands tapped and no untapped blockers. GPT5 Gramps has lethal on board (Phoenix 2 + Visionary 2 + Weaver 3 = 7 damage vs 5 life). While passing moves to combat where lethal attacks are available, failing to play the land first wastes a land drop and leaves mana unavailable for potential combat tricks or post-combat plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main without playing Mountain
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain from hand first, then move to combat and attack with all three creatures for lethal damage (7 vs 5 life with no possible blockers since all opponent's lands are tapped)
